findings.current:
“We’ll set up a perimeter here.”

“What?”

“You mean a perimeter? In this situation?”
findings.defect: “Perimeter” suggests a defensive boundary rather than the enclosing cordon Won intends to use to intercept survivors.
findings.rationale: 포위망 is an encircling formation around a target or route, not merely the perimeter of an area.
findings.replacement:
“We’ll form a cordon here.”

“What?”

“You mean a cordon? In this situation?”

findings.current:
“I won’t waste any more time talking. Hide and form a perimeter. When I give the signal, be ready to kill anyone.”

Won Myunghoon’s voice, thick with killing intent, was no different from a written verdict handed down by the Supreme Court.

Realizing that there would be no appeal, the Guild members scattered and began forming a perimeter.
findings.defect: The repeated “perimeter” continues to frame the formation as defensive rather than as a concealed cordon intended to surround and kill anyone approaching.
findings.rationale: Both occurrences of 포위망 refer to the same ambush formation and require consistent tactical terminology.
findings.replacement:
“I won’t waste any more time talking. Hide and form a cordon. When I give the signal, be ready to kill anyone.”

Won Myunghoon’s voice, thick with killing intent, was no different from a written verdict handed down by the Supreme Court.

Realizing that there would be no appeal, the Guild members scattered and began forming the cordon.
findings.source:
“더 이상 길게 말 안 한다. 숨어서 포위망 펼쳐. 내 신호가 떨어지면 누구든 죽여 버릴 수 있게.”

원명훈의 살기 어린 목소리는 대법원의 판결문이나 다름없었다.

항소 따위는 통하지 않는다는 것을 깨달은 사람들이 뿔뿔이 흩어져 포위망을 형성하기 시작했다.

findings.current: “Team Leader 1—I mean, what should we do about Team Leader 1?”
findings.defect: The draft repeats the same English title and therefore loses the speaker’s deliberate correction from the respectful 팀장님 to the stripped, non-honorific 팀장.
findings.rationale: The mid-sentence withdrawal of respect shows the Guild member adapting to Won Myunghoon’s contempt for Jonghun.
findings.replacement: “Team Leader One, sir—I mean, what should we do about Team Leader One?”

findings.current: *If he opened his mouth, he wouldn’t have survived either.*
findings.defect: The draft turns the source’s euphemistic threat of serious consequences into an explicit assertion that Jonghun would have died.
findings.rationale: 무사하지 못하다 means not emerging unharmed or unscathed; it does not specifically state death.
findings.replacement: *If he opened his mouth, he wouldn’t have gotten off unscathed either.*

findings.current: “What a rude bastard. He really doesn’t hold back with his elders, does he? Right?”
findings.defect: “Doesn’t hold back” weakens the complaint that there is apparently nothing Won will not say to an elder, and the plural “elders” blurs the immediate hierarchy.
findings.rationale: 못 하는 말이 없다 specifically means that no remark is beyond him, while 어른 invokes the respect owed to an older person.
findings.replacement: “What a rude bastard. There’s nothing he won’t say to an elder, is there? Right?”
findings.source: “저 싸가지 없는 새끼. 어른한테 못 하는 말이 없네. 그렇죠?”

findings.current: “It’s not a bad idea in several ways. Since Jin Taekyung is dead, we need at least one A-Rank Hunter on our side to make the picture work.”
findings.defect: “Make the picture work” is an unnatural calque and obscures Won’s point that Jonghun’s death will make their fabricated account look convincing.
findings.rationale: 그림이 살다 refers figuratively to making the overall scenario or appearance credible, not to a literal picture.
findings.replacement: “It works out well in more ways than one. Since Jin Taekyung is dead, we need to throw in an A-Rank Hunter from our side to make the story convincing.”
findings.source: “여러모로 나쁘지 않아. 진태경이 죽었으니 우리 쪽도 A급 하나 정도는 끼워 줘야 그림이 살지.”

findings.current: A single punch smashed apart a thick tree.
findings.defect: “Thick tree” omits the specific scale conveyed by 아름드리나무.
findings.rationale: 아름드리 describes a trunk roughly as broad as a person can encircle with both arms.
findings.replacement: A single punch smashed apart a tree thick enough to wrap both arms around.
findings.source: 일순간 후려친 주먹에 아름드리나무가 박살 났다.

findings.current: “I told you never to bare your teeth at me again.”
findings.defect: The draft unnecessarily repeats “I told you” immediately after the preceding line, “Didn’t I tell you?”, dulling the source’s two-beat threat.
findings.rationale: The Korean completes the preceding question directly without restating 말했다.
findings.replacement: “Never bare your teeth at me again.”

findings.current: At the same time, I drove my tightly clenched fist into his mouth.
findings.defect: The neutral “mouth” sanitizes the deliberately coarse body-part term 아가리.
findings.rationale: 아가리 is a contemptuous, dehumanizing term for the mouth; “maw” preserves that force without adding a new action.
findings.replacement: At the same time, I drove my tightly clenched fist into his maw.
findings.source: 동시에 불끈 쥔 주먹을, 놈의 아가리에 박아넣었다.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, but it mistranslates the ambush formation, loses a meaningful honorific withdrawal, makes an implied consequence explicitly fatal, and has several localized register and prose issues.
